questions.q: In a traditional Bahay Kubo, what is the primary purpose of the silong (the space underneath the house)?
questions.n: The silong serves as a multi-purpose area for storing crops, farming implements, and sheltering livestock.

questions.q: What is the name of the main area in the Bahay Kubo used for living, dining, and sleeping?
questions.n: The bulwagan is the largest room in the house, serving as the social and private core of the home.

questions.q: What is the name of the open or covered area in the Bahay Kubo used for cooking, washing, and laundry, often located near the kitchen?
questions.n: The batalan acts as the service gallery used for wet activities and as a transition to the outdoors.

questions.q: What is the permeable projecting platform in a Bahay Kubo where kitchen utensils and water jars are typically stored?
questions.n: The banggerahan is a slatted rack extending from the window used for drying and storing kitchenware.

questions.q: What is the primary functional purpose of using bamboo slat floors in the bulwagan and batalan areas?
o: Ventilation and to allow spills to pass through
Ease of replacement and material availability
questions.n: The spacing between slats allows cool air to enter from below and liquid waste to fall directly to the ground.

questions.q: What is the characteristic arch design primarily used in Romanesque Architecture?
questions.n: The rounded or semi-circular arch is the most fundamental diagnostic feature of Romanesque design.

questions.q: What are the typical window characteristics found in Romanesque structures?
questions.n: Due to the massive weight of the stone vaults, windows had to be kept small to maintain wall integrity.

questions.q: What is a defining wall characteristic of the Romanesque period?
questions.n: Romanesque walls were built incredibly thick to support the heavy masonry barrel and groin vaults.

questions.q: Romanesque architecture is historically considered a combination of which two architectural eras or styles?
questions.n: Romanesque architecture evolved from Roman building techniques combined with Byzantine decorative and structural influences.

questions.q: What is the most identifying window shape/characteristic of the Romanesque style?
questions.n: The rounded arch window is the definitive aperture shape that characterizes the Romanesque look.

questions.q: Who is the Architect of Record for the Century Pacific Tower project by Arthaland?
questions.n: GF & Partners Architects (GFP) served as the local Architect of Record for this high-end development.

questions.q: The Arthaland Century Pacific Tower holds LEED Platinum and BERDE 5-star ratings; what other specific green building rating did it achieve?
questions.n: The tower made history by becoming the world's first certified EDGE Zero Carbon project.

questions.q: What specific tropical design element was utilized for the building's facade to manage solar heat gain?
questions.n: Vertical fins are used to block low-angle sun and reduce heat while maintaining views.

questions.q: What is the primary occupancy or building type of the Century Pacific Tower?
questions.n: It is designed primarily as a high-grade office building for corporate tenants.

questions.q: What type of glazing system is used in the facade of the Century Pacific Tower to enhance energy efficiency?
questions.n: Double glazing provides an insulating layer that significantly reduces thermal transfer.

questions.q: How many main exterior stairs are integrated into the structure of the Ziggurat of Ur?
questions.n: The ziggurat features three monumental staircases: one central and two flanking along the walls.

questions.q: What was the primary basis for the orientation of the Ziggurat of Ur?
questions.n: The ziggurat's corners are oriented toward the North, South, East, and West.

questions.q: What was the primary religious or functional purpose of the Ziggurat structure?
questions.n: Ziggurats were built as dwelling places for the gods, topped with a temple.

questions.q: What primary material was the Ziggurat of Ur constructed from?
questions.n: The structure consists of a sun-dried mud-brick core with a baked-brick exterior skin.

questions.q: What is the main structural characteristic of the Ziggurat of Ur?
questions.n: The ziggurat is a terraced structure with receding levels, forming a stepped pyramid.

questions.q: What is the primary architectural style associated with the Bauhaus Dessau?
questions.n: The Bauhaus is a seminal example of the International Style or Modern architecture.

questions.q: What primary color scheme was prominently used in the Bauhaus Dessau?
questions.n: These colors reflect the industrial aesthetic and De Stijl influence common at the school.

questions.q: What specific architectural design feature was used in Bauhaus to achieve 'transparency' and lightness in the structure?
questions.n: The glass curtain wall allowed for continuous glazing around corners, creating a sense of weightlessness.

questions.q: What design principle regarding symmetry was typically applied in Bauhaus architecture?
questions.n: Bauhaus buildings like the Dessau campus are asymmetrical, with different wings for different functions.

questions.q: What is the characteristic roof type used in Bauhaus buildings?
questions.n: Flat roofs were a signature of Modernism, often intended for use as terrace gardens.

questions.q: What is the name of the architecture school/fellowship established by Frank Lloyd Wright?
questions.n: Wright founded the Taliesin Fellowship to train apprentices in his architectural philosophy.

questions.q: What is the specific architectural philosophy or style associated with the Fallingwater house?
questions.n: Organic architecture promotes harmony between human habitation and the natural world.

questions.q: Which project is famous for its organic architecture and is considered one of 'America's greatest' works designed by FLW?
questions.n: Fallingwater is widely regarded as Wright's masterpiece and a pinnacle of American architecture.

questions.q: What is the name of the early modern architectural style established and championed by Frank Lloyd Wright?
questions.n: The Prairie style was Wright's first major contribution, focusing on the horizontal plains of the US Midwest.

questions.q: What was the name of the custom-designed concrete blocks reinforced with steel rods used by Wright in his California houses?
questions.n: These patterned blocks were woven together with steel, creating a 'textile' structural system.

questions.q: What type of specification is used when a specific brand name is mandated?
questions.n: A proprietary specification names a specific manufacturer or trade name.

questions.q: What type of specification focuses on prescribing a specific material to be used?
questions.n: Prescriptive specifications describe the materials, equipment, and installation methods in detail.

questions.q: What type of specification focuses on the desired outcome or performance of a material rather than its brand?
questions.n: Performance specs describe the required results and let the contractor choose how to achieve them.

questions.q: What is the general term for a specification that describes the qualities and characteristics of materials?
questions.n: Descriptive specifications give a detailed description of the product's properties without naming brands.

questions.q: What do you call the detailed written documents that define the quality, materials, workmanship, and procedures for a project?
questions.n: Construction specifications are the written requirements for materials, equipment, and systems.

questions.q: Pertaining to SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), what is the term for home-grown plants that are stacked vertically on shelves?
questions.n: Vertical gardening maximizes space by growing crops in upward layers.

questions.q: What is the term for home-grown plants cultivated in pots, containers, or grow bags?
questions.n: Container-based gardening uses portable vessels to grow plants where soil is unavailable.

questions.q: What is the term for home-grown plants that grow in fish water filled with nutrients?
questions.n: Aquaponics uses fish waste as a nutrient source for plants, which in turn filter the water.

questions.q: What is the term for home-grown plants that are sprayed or misted with nutrient-rich water?
questions.n: In aeroponics, roots are kept in an air/mist environment without soil or a liquid pond.

questions.q: What is the term for home-grown plants that are not soil-based and solely rely on water filled with nutrients?
questions.n: Hydroponics is the method of growing plants in a water-based, nutrient-rich solution.

questions.q: Who is the Architect responsible for the creation of plans and specifications?
questions.n: The AOR is legally responsible for the design documents and their compliance with codes.

questions.q: Which architect is primarily responsible for the construction phase?
questions.n: The AICC is responsible for the direct supervision and management of the actual building process.

questions.q: What is the designation for an architect with a specific area of specialization?
questions.n: A PCA is a specialist who provides expert services in a particular field of architecture.

questions.q: What is the designation for an ASEAN Architect working on a local project in collaboration with a local architect?
questions.n: A Foreign Architect must collaborate with a local AOR to practice in a host country.

questions.q: What is the classification of the violation for failure to post the Certificate of Occupancy/Use/Operation?
questions.n: Administrative omissions like failing to display a certificate are typically classified as light violations.

questions.q: What is the classification for a change in existing use or occupancy without a Certificate of Change of Occupancy?
questions.n: Changing occupancy without approval can lead to severe life-safety issues (e.g., fire load changes).

questions.q: What is the classification for the use or occupancy of a building without an appropriate Certificate of Occupancy?
questions.n: Occupying a building before the certificate is issued is considered a Less Grave violation.

questions.q: What is the classification for an unauthorized change in type of construction from more fire-resistive to less fire-resistive?
questions.n: Compromising the fire-resistance of a building is one of the most serious code violations.

questions.q: What is the classification for failure to provide or install appropriate safety measures for the protection of workers and the public?
questions.n: Safety measures like nets or signs fall under this classification, though they are critical for worker safety.

questions.q: What is a Roman structure with seating all around, primarily used for gladiator fights?
questions.n: The amphitheater is an elliptical or circular structure with central arenas for public spectacles.
